newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch forwarders voice concern over fuel surcharge.
newsitem.headline: Dutch forwarders voice concern over fuel surcharge.

text.p: Dutch forwarders and shippers are united in their concerns over the imposition of "over night" surcharges, said Hans Knuvers, spokesman for the Dutch freight forwarders association, ATAN.
"Everybody is complaining but at the same time we recognise that the fuel prices have increased" and we need better guidelines concerning any future rates increases or surcharges, Knuvers said..
"In the past the industry was regulated by competition rules from Brussels and IATA. But now there are no real guidelines, so this has resulted in the current situation," he added.
The main objection of the Dutch forwarders is the short notice, he added. "We have the same concerns as the shippers," he said.
But Knuvers said he was resigned to the fact that there is little that can be done concerning the present round of increases.

Commenting on calls by some shippers to ban carriers that implement surcharges, Knuvers said that as soon as the Dutch national carrier, KLM, announced its surcharge of 20 Dutch guilder cents per kilo, most of the other carriers followed, therefore such a move is impractical, he added.
"We can only meet with the airlines and voice our disapproval," Knuvers said.

"Surcharges are never a nice thing but we are definitely looking for better guidelines in the future so this can be avoided and we are in regular contact with the shippers." -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
